howToUpdate: Curated by mgmt-ops. Schema and rules: header of tools/lib/progress.mjs. Check: node tools/console.mjs progress --check. Plain words in title/fixes/felt/gate/next/why; jargon in details. Every phone number carries its tag (OBSERVED/CONFIRMED), driver and ref. No URLs, addresses or names.
goal: On the iPhone, scrolling with your finger should feel smooth: no frame slower than 50 ms (a visible hitch) and a steady 60 frames per second.

complaints.text: the top of the page (hero) and scrolling out of it feel laggy
the end of the page (pushing past the end, where the bottom panel grows) feels laggy

changes.text: Coming up for you: a sitting on the phone that compares the original page with today's best build (the countdown fix and F3 together).

The robot finger turned out to play every stroke as a quick flick, so its results so far don't count (tool problem I-042). The countdown fix's robot test (P-032) was void; all robot-finger tests wait for the tool fix. The phone runs the carousel test (P14) meanwhile.
Touch-listener blind test scored: neither you nor the second tester felt a difference (2 of 4 pairs each, the same as guessing).
Phone tests approved and queued: the avatar carousel at the top (P14) and the softer blur easing for the card reveal (P-038).
The iOS Simulator was checked as a stand-in for the phone: not usable as a judge of smoothness. The real iPhone stays the judge.
Your three blind swipe pairs for the countdown fix all came back 'same'. It now lands only if the robot-finger test (P-032) passes.
Layout containment (lc-cq3) dropped: the work moved elsewhere, the slow frames did not get shorter.
F3 removed the 106-118 ms hitch in the middle of the page in 4 of 4 scripted runs; the F1 variant stopped.

items.title: Countdown fix: digits stop repainting when the end panel moves
items.fixes: At the end of the page, each time the bottom panel starts to grow or shrink, the countdown's ~80 digit layers were repainted. This one CSS rule keeps the digits inside the panel's own layer, so that repaint is gone.

best.what: frames over 50 ms while the panel moves, per run
best.note: threshold-sensitive: at 54 ms one control run also has 0

best.what: frames over 34 ms while the panel moves, per run
median frame time while the panel moves

felt.text: 3 blind swipe pairs on the real page; one was a same-vs-same check, which you passed. You did not prefer the fix in either real pair.

items.gate: P-032: with a robot finger on the phone, the fix must show fewer slow frames at the start of the panel motion than without it, in every run.
items.next: P-032 again, as a fresh run, once the robot-finger tool is fixed (I-042). If it passes, it lands; if not, it does not land: harmless, but nothing you would feel.
details: Build mw10e-cdwc = aw1-10e + CSS 5dc6e8e37388 (panel digit faces will-change: auto); branch fix/mw10e-cdwc, review-cdwc round 2 resolved B1/B2/B4/B5, B3 = P-032.

P-029 (g vs g-cdwc, driver M, 4v4 runs): face-repaint frames 85 % -> 0 %, layers at the hold 113 -> 33, excess per forward tween 209-234 -> 79-146 ms. >34 not threshold-sensitive; >50 threshold-sensitive (>54 twin 0/1/3/20 vs 0).
Second phone block (arch-sim reference FP-3, same driver M, g vs g-cdwc): >50 ms 1-24 -> 0, >34 ms 45-52 -> 0-1 per run.
Mechanism: WebKit repaints a whole layer when its device-pixel-rounded subpixel offset changes (CONFIRMED by source); that the 80 repaints are this stays OBSERVED.
Swipe pairs: C-001 (pair 3) and two earlier pairs; 0/2 preferences for the fix, catch pair passed.
P-032 attempt 1 VOID (0 valid runs): I-042, G strokes play as ~50 ms flicks, so all G data so far is invalid. After the I-042 fix, P-032 runs first as a fresh block.

items.title: F3: touch listeners set up once, removing the hitch in the middle
items.fixes: One very slow frame (over 100 ms) in the middle of the page, around 1960 px down, when the end-of-page panel added its touch listeners. F3 adds them once when the page loads, so that frame is gone.

best.what: the slow frame around 1960 px down
best.after: none over 34 ms in 4 of 4 runs
best.note: one unexplained 49 ms frame at 2019 px in 1 run

best.what: frames over 50 ms in the whole scroll, per run

items.next: P-036 on the phone once the robot-finger tool is fixed (I-042, right after P-032), then review, then your blind swipe test.

P-022 block B: edge frame (y 1940-2010) C 106-118 ms vs F3 none > 34 ms in 4/4; dt>50 in y 1700-2200 1/1/1/1 vs 0/0/0/0 (threshold-sensitive, the 46 ms twin overlaps); scroll dt>50 C 2/1/2/3 vs 1/0/0/1.
Chrome regression A/B within noise on every row, 0 errors/404s, 0.13 % pixel diff.
Strokes that start on the nav header are not covered by the robot test: only your finger test checks them.

items.title: Card reveal ends without a page re-layout (re-keep-op)
items.fixes: Just below the hero, the people card that fades in caused a whole-page layout as its reveal ended. This keeps the card in its own layer at rest, so those end-of-reveal layouts go away.

best.what: the frame at the end of the card reveal
best.note: measured on re-keep, the parent build; 2 runs each

items.gate: P-033 gain block on the phone: fewer frames over 34 ms in the reveal, in every run.
items.next: P-033 gain block. Frames over 50 ms can't move here (there are none in this window), so even a pass would likely be bundled with the next combined wave, not landed alone.

checks.what: phone gain block (its step 0 safety check passed)

details: re-keep-op = re-keep + revealed card resting at opacity 0.999 / blur(0px) / translateY(0) (CSS 507f0ca4); predicted to also remove the +700 frame.
P-019: re-keep +900 frame 33 -> 17 ms (17/17 vs 33/33), +1150 shrink-frame Layout gone (dt 28-31 vs 39-41). Mechanism CONFIRMED by source (presence flip, F-075); on the phone OBSERVED.
P-033 step 0 PASS 14:47Z: card composited in both arms, idle paint over the card 4.77 vs 4.89 ms per cycle.

items.title: Card reveal blur with a standard easing curve (PoC 2)
items.fixes: The card's blur fade uses an easing type that iPhone Safari freezes while the page is busy (CONFIRMED). The same curve written as a standard easing keeps moving and may make each reveal frame cheaper.
items.gate: P-038: on the phone, the reveal frames must cost less (composite and style time) in every run.
items.next: P-038 on the phone, after the P-033 block.

checks.what: phone block: is each reveal frame cheaper?

details: blur-cubic: T10 linear() tails of the reveal/hide blur replaced by exact cubic-bezier splits of cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) 1.6 s (CSS 069725e4); max difference 0.64 px of blur.
F-080 CONFIRMED: on the phone linear() freezes during main-thread blocks; cubic-bezier and sampled WAAPI keep moving. Reveal only; the hide tail is not measured yet.

items.title: Avatar carousel: each tick re-lays out the whole page
items.fixes: The small rotating profile pictures near the top (the 'blinking small profiles' you noticed) cost a 25-30 ms whole-page layout about once a second, even when you are not scrolling.
items.gate: P14: find which part of the carousel change escapes to the whole page.

checks.what: P14: does keeping the pictures mounted stop the whole-page layout?

details: Rest attribution (P-033 step 0, OBSERVED): 40/41 rotator callbacks dirty a whole-view Layout 1-5 ms later, 12.8-43.6 ms, median 25-26 ms.

P14 arms: C aw1-10e, V1 st4-noswap (pictures updated in place, no insert/remove; probe only), V2 re-contain-js (#people as a layout boundary). Pre-registered: V1 'gone' = 25 % or fewer view-rooted ticks.

items.title: Countdown ticking at rest (PoC 3)
items.fixes: At rest at the top of the page, the countdown ticks every second, and some ticks make a slow frame. This first finds which part of the tick is slow; then the digits could run on the GPU instead.
items.gate: P-037: name the slow part of the tick before any build.
items.next: P-037 attribution run on the phone. A build only after the countdown fix (cdwc) lands.
details: Any countdown-ca ticket carries the P-034 / F-076 gate: GPU animations on the digit faces might bring back the ~80 layers that cdwc removes (UNRESOLVED).

items.fixes: Nine smaller fixes from wave 1 (scroll handlers, idle countdown work, animations, the scroll engine), combined. Every new fix is built and measured on top of it.

items.title: iOS Simulator as a stand-in for the phone
items.why: The Simulator does not show the phone's slow frames for most kinds of frame, so it can't judge smoothness. At most it hints where to look; the real iPhone stays the judge.
